title: Sintered regolith as a habitat construction material: strength, energy per tonne and mass per m2
question: What do peer-reviewed materials-science studies and NASA/ESA technical documentation establish about sintering lunar and Martian regolith into construction elements: achievable compressive and tensile strength, porosity, thermal-cycling and vacuum durability, sintering temperature and energy per tonne? What do habitat shielding and structural-mass studies imply for the 0.8 t/m2 sintered-regolith and 0.06 t/m2 steel allocation in NOXIA's habitat bill of materials? Specifically, is sintered regolith defensible as a pressure-retaining habitat shell, or only as shielding, paving or non-structural infill, and what energy per tonne and mass per m2 follow for a habitat of a given floor area and shape?
why_now: NOXIA-MAT-0001 introduced material bills on 28.10.2026. lib/game/construction/materials.ts now carries the provisional off-world habitat row (regolith 0.8 t/m2, steel 0.06 t/m2) and marks all quantities as provisional; coordination/open/20261028-0042 explicitly asks the Knowledge Graph for 'Regolith als Baustoff (Sintern, Energie je t)'. These values already feed building cost display and the Mars/Moon worldbuilding, so an evidence-backed range would replace an asserted number now.
real_world_anchor: Sintering of lunar and Martian regolith simulants; mechanical, thermal and vacuum durability of sintered regolith; habitat shielding mass and embodied-energy budgets.
novelty_reason: No previous topic addresses materials processing or structural engineering. RES-20260828-49AF01DE asks which bodies contain which resources and at what ore grade; it does not establish whether regolith can be sintered into a pressure shell, what strength it reaches, or how much energy and mass per m2 a habitat requires. RES-20260828-79092FF4 covers per-capita consumables and hazards, not construction mass.
